teaser.text: Automatic Data Processing, or ADP, helps employers pay and manage their workforces. Its business looks simple from the outside—software, payroll and benefits—but the money moves through several distinct channels.

blocks.heading: Where could ADP's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is $273.19 (+0%) in October 2027 and $301.74 (+16%) in October 2029, with bear/base/bull probabilities of 23%/58%/19%; the three-year range is $201.24 to $419.11. The outcome turns on service growth, client-funds income, and whether Lyric, WorkForce Suite, and Global Payroll bookings become active customers through accurate migrations with lower service effort. The October 28, 2026 results are the next test of hiring, retention, margins, and fiscal 2027 guidance. The investment case depends on service growth and platform execution, not client-funds income alone.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for ADP?

paragraphs.text: The base path follows management’s 5%–6% revenue and 9%–11% adjusted EPS guidance, with gradual operating leverage. The first year also aligns with the analysts’ next-twelve-month estimate, which implies roughly $4.9bn of earnings at about 400m shares. The bear case reflects 0%–1% pays-per-control growth, weaker retention, lower client-funds income and PEO margin pressure. The bull case requires bookings from Lyric, WorkForce Suite and global payroll to convert into customers and lower service effort. The forecast excludes unusual alignment and settlement charges.

blocks.heading: How much cash does ADP really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation adds another economic cost. ADP recorded $242.6 million of stock pay without an equivalent current cash payment. Deducting it gives analytical real free cash flow of $4,533.5 million. Client payroll money belongs in a separate reconciliation, because it should not be subtracted again from corporate operating cash.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for ADP today?

paragraphs.text: Enterprise value estimates the cost of acquiring the operating business after accounting for debt and usable corporate cash. Client funds are different: ADP held about $44.0 billion for clients and owed about $44.4 billion against those balances. A buyer cannot spend that money. The table brings together the current price, valuation measures and cash yields that frame the purchase.

blocks.heading: How much does ADP pay per share?

blocks.heading: Does ADP's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Fiscal 2026 makes the policy clear. ADP paid $2,626.3 million in dividends and spent $2,083.3 million on buybacks. Together, those payments absorbed $4,709.6 million. That was 98.6% of free cash flow. The January 2026 authorization for $6 billion of future repurchases was permission to buy shares, not an immediate cash payment.

paragraphs.text: The forecast would move toward the bear case if bookings convert slowly, pays per control remains near zero growth, or retention falls beyond the guided decline. Client-funds yields and balances would also matter, as would PEO pass-through growth through FY2029.

blocks.heading: What is ADP's dividend yield at its share price?

paragraphs.text: At $280.32, ADP trades at 25.6x trailing and 22.9x forward earnings, against a 4.3% free cash flow yield and 2.4% dividend yield. Revenue growth slowed from 9.9% in fiscal 2022 to 6.7% in fiscal 2026, while operating margin and the company’s own real free cash flow rose as shares of revenue. U.S. pays per control growth was 1.0% in fiscal 2026.

earnings.title: ADP earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: ADP next reports on October 28, 2026, with guidance for steady revenue growth, higher margins and faster adjusted EPS growth.
earnings.opening: ADP’s next results are expected on October 28, 2026. Watch whether customer activity, profitable growth and efficiency support the annual promise.
earnings.closing: The full ADP memo also covers ADP’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has ADP guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: On July 29, 2026, ADP forecast revenue growth of 5.0%–6.0% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 9.0%–11.0%. Adjusted diluted earnings per share means profit per share after specified exclusions, while allowing for potential additional shares. ADP also expects adjusted EBIT margin to expand by 70–90 basis points. That means keeping more operating profit from each dollar of revenue, so efficiency can do some of the work that hiring cannot.

The employment assumptions are restrained. Pays per control, which measures employee growth inside existing payroll customers, should rise only 0.0%–1.0%. Employer Services bookings should grow 4.0%–7.0%, but a booking is only a new commitment. A customer that signs for payroll software may produce little revenue until ADP installs and activates the service. Retention is also expected to weaken by 10–30 basis points, leaving pricing, new customers and efficiency to carry more of the forecast.

blocks.heading: Did ADP keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management’s public guidance provides another test. It forecast revenue growth of 5%–6% for fiscal 2026. It forecast adjusted earnings-per-share growth of 8%–10%. It delivered 7% revenue growth and 11% adjusted earnings-per-share growth. Those results support a record of delivery, although guidance and the internal bonus scorecard use different definitions.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in ADP’s next release?

paragraphs.text: The most revealing comparison will be between customer activity and financial growth. If earnings strengthen while hiring remains subdued, client-funds interest, service efficiency and the share count may explain why. In PEO Services, revenue excluding benefits pass-throughs should be compared with segment profit, because higher benefits charges can enlarge revenue without improving the underlying service.
